answer: Price new identities on a rising curve. Each registration burns a fee that compounds 1% above the previous one and decays back toward the base over a few epochs, much as EIP-1559 reprices gas under load. A lone agent sailing into a quiet harbor pays the base, but an operator planting a thousand-key orchard pays over 140 times base for the 500th seedling alone, so a grove of fakes costs more than it can harvest, and burned fees can't be recycled into the next farm.
